name: Mënsch
description: MÃ«nsch is a Swiss Jass game for four players in partnerships. It belongs to the Jass family of games popular in Switzerland and surrounding regions. The game features the 'Mensch' (Queen of Clubs) as a permanent highest trump, similar to other games in the Ombre/Solo family. Players bid for the right to choose trumps and must make their contract.

history.origins: MÃ«nsch is a Swiss Jass game, part of the larger Jass family that originated in the Netherlands and spread to Switzerland. It shares ancestry with games like Ombre and Solo.
timeline: Traditional: Developed within Swiss Jass tradition
19th-20th Century: Played in Swiss card clubs and homes
Present: Still played in Switzerland as part of the Jass repertoire
history.cultural: Jass games are a significant part of Swiss cultural identity, played in pubs, clubs, and homes throughout the country.
history.evolution: The game follows the classic Jass structure with bidding, trump selection, and trick-taking, with unique Swiss scoring conventions.

setup.players: 4 players in fixed partnerships, partners sitting opposite each other.
setup.deck: 36-card Jass deck (6 through Ace in four suits: Acorns, Shields, Flowers, Bells). Can use standard deck with 5s and below removed. Ranking in trumps: Under (Jack), 9, Ace, King, Ober (Queen), Banner (10), 8, 7, 6. In non-trump: Ace, King, Ober, Under, Banner, 9, 8, 7, 6.
setup.dealing: 9 cards to each player, dealt in packets of 3.
setup.equipment: 36-card Jass deck or modified standard deck, score sheet.

rules.objective: Win the majority of points in tricks. The team that wins the bid must make their contract.
rules.gameplay: Must follow suit if possible. If unable to follow, must play a trump if available. Highest trump wins, or highest card of led suit if no trumps.
keyRules: Must trump if void in led suit (in most variants)
Under of trumps (Puur) is highest card

strategy.basic: Remember the special trump ranking (Under and 9 are highest). Try to capture the Puur and Nell. Support your partner's efforts.
strategy.intermediate: Bid based on hand strength and distribution. Void yourself in weak suits. Save trumps for when you need them.
strategy.advanced: Card counting is essential. Track trumps and high cards. Coordinate with partner through card play signals. Understand when to sacrifice tricks.
tips: The Puur (trump Under) is the most powerful card - use it wisely
The Nell (trump 9) is also extremely valuable
Try to win the last trick for the 5-point bonus
If defending, coordinate with partner to stop the declarer

scoring.description: Points are awarded based on cards captured and whether the contract was made. Target is majority of 157 points (81+).
scoring.winCondition: Win at least 81 of the 157 available points.
